clinician.final_diagnosis: low-grade appendiceal mucinous neoplasm with fifteen negative lymph nodes
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 33-year-old man presented with lower abdominal pain and fullness after abdominal trauma and a palpable mass in the right lower quadrant. Abdominal MRI revealed a large, thin-walled, intraperitoneal cystic lesion adjacent to the cecal pole with the appendix not separately identified (E001). Intraoperatively, a large inflammatory lesion with enlarged lymph nodes was found in the mesentery of the ascending colon and a right hemicolectomy with primary anastomosis was performed (E005). The patient's postoperative course was unremarkable with full recovery (E007). Although histopathology report is not directly documented in the source, the known final diagnosis states it revealed a completely excised low-grade appendiceal mucinous neoplasm with fifteen negative lymph nodes.
